SAMtools, BCFtools and HTSlib 1.21 – samtools, bcftools (with its plugins built in), bgzip, tabix and htsfile: the
programs of the modules samtools/1.21, bcftools/1.21, htslib/1.21 and tabix/1.21

Licences: SAMtools and BCFtools MIT/Expat (notices/1.21/LICENSE.samtools, LICENSE.bcftools – BCFtools would be under
the GNU GPL only if it were built with the GNU Scientific Library, and it is not); HTSlib MIT/Expat and modified
3-clause BSD (notices/1.21/LICENSE.htslib), with htscodecs (BSD: notices/1.21/LICENSE.htscodecs.md). Part of every
program: zlib 1.3.1 (notices/shared/zlib-LICENSE), bzip2 1.0.8 (notices/shared/bzip2-LICENSE), liblzma of XZ 5.4.6
(public domain: notices/shared/xz-COPYING; the GNU licences next to it are those of other parts of XZ, which are not
compiled in) and Emscripten's runtime (MIT and NCSA: notices/shared/LICENSE.emscripten).

Upstream source: the release archives samtools-1.21.tar.bz2, bcftools-1.21.tar.bz2 and htslib-1.21.tar.bz2
(https://github.com/samtools/samtools/releases/tag/1.21, and likewise bcftools and htslib), with zlib, bzip2 and XZ –
their addresses, sizes and SHA-256 are in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/tools/hts/versions.lock.json.

Compiled to WebAssembly by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit
170e9f0, 21 October 2026) with Emscripten 3.1.64: one thread, 32-bit pointers with 64-bit file offsets and positions,
at most 2 GiB of memory. Not compiled in: reading remote files (HTTP, FTP, S3, GCS), HTSlib's plugins, libdeflate, the
curses screen of samtools tview (its text and HTML output, -d T and -d H, are there), Perl filters, and the command
bcftools polysomy, which needs the GNU Scientific Library (upstream's default build leaves it out too). bcftools has
all 39 plugins of the release, among them +split-vep, +fill-tags, +trio-dnm2, +trio-stats, +trio-switch-rate,
+parental-origin and +mendelian2 (the successor of 1.16's +mendelian, which 1.21 no longer has); bcftools plugin -l
lists them.

The files here are those of dist/hts-1.21/ in the project's tested release package hts-1.21-wasm.zip (SHA-256
6a814bb96c007a4cb623c3d8d684688312d1e50d107a4e379586f40e0f52b62c), made by its workflow "Build and validate HTS
toolchains" (.github/workflows/hts.yml, run 39672984182), unchanged: bcftools, samtools, bgzip, tabix and htsfile
(.mjs and .wasm), builtin-plugins.json (the plugins, with the SHA-256 of their sources), build-manifest.json (the
compiler, the build's inputs and the SHA-256 of every file) and notices/. Left out: the package's HTSlib SDK (headers
and static libraries for compiling other programs), its copies of the source archives, its runner (runtime/hts.mjs),
tests and test data.

Changes to the source (all in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/tools/hts/, with README.md and PORTABILITY.md
saying why): the plugins are compiled into bcftools – prepare-plugins.py compiles each plugin as upstream's Makefile
does, gives its symbols a prefix of its own, and puts a table where bcftools loads a shared library; the plugins' code
and options are upstream's. Counters and offsets that the release keeps in a "long" (64 bits on Linux, 32 in
WebAssembly) are made 64-bit, as on Linux: the depth totals of bcftools stats, the consensus caller of bcftools call
-c, the offsets of bgzip -b and -s, the optical-duplicate coordinates and library size of samtools markdup, the
subsampling seed of samtools view; and +GTisec allocates its table at its real size.

Checked by the project against SAMtools, BCFtools and HTSlib 1.21 built natively from the same archives, unchanged,
with the plugins as shared libraries: 61 of 61 cases – every plugin with real input, the core commands of bcftools,
samtools, bgzip, tabix and htsfile, and the 64-bit counters and offsets – with the same results in Node.js, Chromium,
Firefox and WebKit (values compared exactly; only version and command-line headers, BGZF block layout and the paths of
the files set aside); both versions in one browser workspace; and the package itself, unzipped, in all four.

In the terminal: assets/js/hts-re.js runs the version of the module that is loaded (as PATH decides on the Research
Environment; 1.21 if modules are not required and none is loaded), each command in a worker of its own
(assets/js/threads-worker.mjs) with the files its arguments name, their indexes, and the files named in a list
(samtools merge -b, bcftools concat -f …) or inside an option's value (bcftools view -i 'ID=@ids.txt', -S
^samples.txt). With nothing piped into it, a command reads from the terminal: bcftools view or samtools view with no
file prints its usage, as upstream. bgzip asks before it overwrites a file; a program here cannot wait for the answer,
so it is no, and the terminal says so (bgzip -f overwrites). Options that ask for threads (samtools -@, --threads;
bcftools --threads; bgzip -@) are left out with a note: every command runs on one thread. gzip, gunzip and zcat keep
the bgzip of the shared program runner (../../../biowasm/htslib/1.17/), as in the workbench.

The Research Environment has the same versions: samtools/1.21, bcftools/1.21, htslib/1.21 and tabix/1.21.
